title: Ecosystem Services: a Method for Sustainable Development
provider: University of Geneva (UNIGE) on Coursera — developed with the Geneva Water Hub and the Natural Capital Project
language: Taught in English; 22 subtitle languages available on Coursera (Russian subtitles included among them). Original content and assessments are in English.
cost: Free to audit the lecture/video content; the verified certificate is paid (subscription or one-off purchase, included with Coursera Plus). Financial aid is available. A free trial is offered.
certificate: Shareable Coursera certificate upon completion of graded assignments — requires payment (or financial aid). Auditing gives content access without the certificate.
duration: Approximately 17 hours total to complete (self-paced). Coursera markets it as ~2 weeks at 10 h/week; UNIGE lists "about 17 hours." Video load by module: ~89 min, 174 min, 76 min, 104 min, 105 min across the five core modules.
target_audience: Learners in environmental sustainability, policy-making, natural-resource management, conservation, and GIS/spatial-analysis applications — students, professionals, and decision-makers. Not designed specifically for SMB agricultural practitioners; oriented toward policy and academic/professional learners.
format: MOOC: video lectures (the dominant format), readings/supporting case-study materials, module quizzes, peer-reviewed essay assignments, discussion prompts, an interactive "TRADE-OFF" serious game, and expert interviews. Self-paced with flexible deadlines.
assessment: Module quizzes (multiple choice), peer-reviewed short essays (e.g. on valuation and on mainstreaming), and graded assignments (mix of auto/AI-graded and peer-evaluated). Certificate requires passing the graded items.
hands_on: Mostly conceptual rather than hands-on. The standout practical element is the optional Module 6 "Create Your Own Ecosystem Services Case": learners do GIS-based hydrological modeling of water ecosystem services using QGIS + the InVEST package, with data preparation/preprocessing, climate-change scenario building, and results interpretation (Kenya's Tana River basin case study). The TRADE-OFF serious game is the other interactive element. Reviewers explicitly note the hands-on technical training is limited relative to the conceptual depth.
tools: QGIS (open-source GIS), InVEST (Integrated Valuation of Ecosystem Services and Tradeoffs — open-source spatial modeling toolkit from the Natural Capital Project), and remote-sensing/open spatial data (elevation, climate, land-use). The TRADE-OFF online serious game.

syllabus.module: Module 1 — Frontiers in Ecosystem Services (~89 min video; 7 readings, 1 quiz)
syllabus.topics: Introduction and key questions; the TRADE-OFF serious game; context and applications of the ES method; weaknesses and limitations of the approach; links between biodiversity, ecosystem services and sustainability; case studies (hydroelectric dams, watershed investments); expert interviews.

syllabus.module: Module 2 — Valuation of Ecosystem Services (~174 min video)
syllabus.topics: Valuation vs monetization; price vs value; economic valuation theory and discount rates; critiques and biases in monetization; indigenous and local knowledge systems; non-monetary valuation approaches; climate-change impacts on agriculture; the 'pricing nature' debate.

syllabus.module: Module 3 — Understanding the Normative Dimensions (~76 min video)
syllabus.topics: History of the ES concept (events, places, people behind it); neoliberalism and ideological underpinnings; participation and social justice in decision-making; power issues and stakeholder engagement; implementation across policy scales.

syllabus.module: Module 4 — Quantitative and Spatially-Explicit Assessment (~104 min video)
syllabus.topics: Data collection and remote sensing; modeling and mapping ecosystem services; scenario planning and prediction; case studies at global, European, national and local scales; tools and software applications.

syllabus.module: Module 5 — Mainstreaming Ecosystem Services into Decision-Making (~105 min video)
syllabus.topics: Governance and regulatory frameworks; enabling factors for successful implementation; private-sector integration; sustainable finance; role of international organizations (e.g. IPBES); regional case studies (Europe, Peru, Mekong Basin).

syllabus.module: Module 6 — Create Your Own Ecosystem Services Case (optional, ~1 hr, hands-on)
syllabus.topics: Practical GIS modeling of water ecosystem services with QGIS + InVEST; data preparation and preprocessing; hydrological modeling; climate-change scenario development; results interpretation. Kenya Tana River basin case study.

strengths: Interdisciplinary balance: deliberately covers scientific/technical, economic, and socio-political dimensions of one method rather than siloing them — a coherent 'one method, many lenses' spine.
Critical honesty: a whole module (and explicit lecture) on the weaknesses, biases, and ideological baggage of the ecosystem-services approach — builds critical thinking instead of selling a tool.
Strong use of real case studies (dams, watersheds, Peru, Mekong, Tana River) and expert interviews — concrete, place-based grounding.
Serious game (TRADE-OFF) as an engaging entry point that lets learners feel trade-offs before formal theory.
Optional applied GIS capstone built entirely on $0 open-source tools (QGIS + InVEST) producing a learner's own case — exactly the zero-cost, reproducible model FOLUR targets.
High production quality and clear instruction; 4.8/5 across 742 reviews, ~98% satisfaction, ~48k enrolled.
Includes non-monetary and indigenous/local knowledge valuation — pluralistic, not just economics.
weaknesses: Heavily video-centric; reviewers complain videos are long and the format is monotonous, with too few readings paired to lectures.
Limited hands-on technical practice: many learners wanted real data-gathering and valuation method practice; the only deep practical work (GIS) is a short optional module.
Some content felt outdated (noted as of 2024).
Structure feels fragmented to some — scattered case studies without a strong, explicit theoretical scaffold tying them together.
A few interview segments judged poorly executed.
Intermediate level and policy/academic framing — not tailored to SMB practitioners; English-only assessments limit accessibility for Russian-speaking agro audiences.
borrow_for_folur: 'One method, multiple lenses' module spine: structure a FOLUR module so the same regional case (e.g. a Kostanay/СКО watershed or degraded pasture) is examined through technical, economic, and socio-political lenses in sequence — gives coherence the reviewers found missing when cases are scattered.

Open-source applied capstone on a $0 stack: replicate the QGIS+InVEST 'create your own case' as a Colab+QGIS notebook where SMB learners model a real North-Kazakhstan basin/landscape with open data — directly matches the FOLUR Python+QGIS+GEE+Colab stack and produces a tangible artifact.

A dedicated 'weaknesses and limitations' lecture per method: teach where ecosystem-service valuation, remote-sensing indices, etc. fail — builds practitioner judgement and scientific honesty (aligns with FOLUR's integrity constraint of not overselling).

Serious-game / trade-off simulation as a hook: a lightweight interactive 'land-use trade-off' exercise (e.g. crop vs grazing vs restoration on a real СКО parcel) before formal theory, to make abstract trade-offs felt.

Pluralistic valuation including non-monetary and local knowledge: explicitly incorporate indigenous/local knowledge and non-monetary value — adapt to Kazakh pastoral/community valuation rather than economics-only.

Real place-based case studies throughout (the course's strongest praised feature): mandate that every FOLUR lecture anchors in a concrete North-Kazakhstan case with real maps/data, never abstract examples.

FIX the format weakness FOLUR can avoid: pair each short video/lecture with a concise reading and an immediate small task, instead of long talking-head videos — directly answers this course's top criticism.
Make the practical work core, not optional: the #1 learner complaint is too little hands-on; FOLUR should make the GIS/data exercise mandatory and central for its practitioner audience.
Offer full Russian-language delivery (lectures + assessments in Cyrillic), not just subtitles, to remove the accessibility barrier this course leaves for non-English audiences.
unverified_notes: Coursera's marketing said '89 total hours of lectures' — this is contradicted by the UNIGE official page and per-module figures (89 MINUTES of video in Module 1; ~17 hours total course). Treated as a Coursera-page extraction artifact; the ~17-hour total is the reliable figure.
Coursera markets '2 weeks at 10 hours/week' (=20h) while UNIGE states 'about 17 hours'; both are platform estimates and roughly consistent.
Exact current price of the certificate not captured (Coursera shows it behind subscription/region-specific pricing); reported only as 'paid / included with Coursera Plus / financial aid available'.
